key_insight: This paper argues that robot policies need explicit 3D geometry, not just 2D vision or latent features, to reliably understand how actions affect objects in the physical world. The proposed Geometric Action Model aims to make robot behavior more grounded for contact-rich manipulation.
problem_solved: Current vision-language-action and video world-action models often learn from 2D image frames or 2D-derived embeddings, which leaves the 3D spatial relationships needed for precise robot manipulation implicit. This makes it harder for robots to reason about object pose, camera viewpoint, and action effects in cluttered, contact-heavy tasks.
method: Introduces a geometric action representation that incorporates 3D spatial structure into robot policy learning.
Connects user instructions, visual perception, and robot control through explicit reasoning about objects, cameras, and actions in 3D space.
Designed to improve manipulation performance by grounding policy decisions in physical geometry rather than only semantic or temporal cues.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this points toward robot policies that are more robust, interpretable, and transferable in real-world manipulation settings. It is especially relevant for tasks where 2D perception alone is insufficient, such as grasping, pushing, and tool use.

paper_title: Geometric Action Model for Robot Policy Learning
paper_authors: Jisang Han, Seonghu Jeon, Jaewoo Jung, René Zurbrügg, Honggyu An
